text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Farmers received only half of the diesel oil needed for farming work in October.
TINERETUL LIBER

- This year's sunflower crop will be enough to meet domestic demand for edible oil and Romania will be able to also export 230,000 tonnes of raw or refined sunflower oil. Maize crops are also sufficient, but sugar beets will not be enough to meet domestic sugar consumption needs.
AZI
- Navol SA ship builder built a 3,000 dwt cargo vessel for a Dutch partner.
- The nine-month trade balance deficit stands at $588.5 million, according to latest statistics.
LIBERTATEA
- Year-on-year inflation rate is higher than expected, while wages and purchasing power have fallen.
- Romanians who got their shareholder certificates under the mass selloff can trade their shares on the over-the-counter market, which opened last week.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania's five regional private investment funds will turn into investment companies starting November 1.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romanian agriculture supplies most of the crops needed to meet domestic consumption requirements, Agriculture Minister Alexandru Lapusan says in an interview.
General:

The three major newspapers publish an opinion poll by the IRSOP institute made only for the use of the ruling PDSR in which President Iliescu leads his main rival, Emil Constantinescu, by only three precent and the PDSR trails the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) by six percent.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Opposition parties signed an accord to oversee the November 3 elections to prevent the PDSR from repeating the electoral fraud of 1946 which allowed the Communists to take power.
- The newspaper presents a list of actions by the PDSR and President Iliescu during the electoral campaign which the paper says amounts to an attempt to chear in Sunday's elections.
ADEVARUL
- The newspaper publishes the debate organised by the newspaper with nine of the 16 presidential candidates.
- The PDSR is ot hold a rally attended by President Iliescu on October 31.

- An opinion poll by the CURS institute shows 25 percent of the people aged up to 29 would vote for Petre Roman, the presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Union (USD), 20 percent for Constantinescu and 16 percent for Iliescu.

- The leading Romanian player Victor Rebengiuc was fired from the Bucharest Bulandra theater after he refused to perform in a play for the ruling PDSR and turn into an campaigning agent for the party.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Doina Cornea, Romania's leading dissident in the communist era, urges the people to vote for one of the three major opposition blocs -- the CDR, the USD or the National Liberal Alliance (ANL).

- The newspaper accuses the PDSR of engaging in mass fraud -- illegal registration of presidential candidates, the attempt to allow the use of voters' cards instead of identification papers, confusion over observers and the appointment of PDSR supporters to administer polling stations.
AZI
- Antonie Iorgovan, mastermind of Romania's post-communist Constitution, says Iliescu is not promoting capable people but has surrounded himself only with people loyal to him.
ZIUA
- The newspaper publishes a message by Romania's ex-King Michael urging Romanians to turn out and vote on November 3.
- A survey by the IMAS institute says 81.2 percent of 17 million eligible voters will turn out on Sunday.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Dan Ioan Popescu, head of the PDSR's Bucharest branch, says in a full-page interview that the party programme solves Romania's problems.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- The newspaper publishes a report by the Romanian Intelligence Service on former Prime Minister Petre Roman's alleged trading with gold.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- President Iliescu, Roman and Constantinescu present their programmes on the issues of culture and education. ($=3,341 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
